notes: 12 upper-division courses plus the undergraduate language requirement. Structure and course lists verified against the live catalog page.

buckets.label: Undergraduate language requirement (non-English language proficiency)
buckets.note: Proficiency in a non-English natural language; satisfied by coursework or examination. Non-course proficiency requirement. Satisfied by ANY of: (1) passing the Linguistics Dept reading + oral proficiency exam in French, German, Italian, Russian, Spanish, Arabic, Farsi, Tagalog, Portuguese, Vietnamese, or ASL; (2) completing the fourth quarter (or beyond) of instruction in any single non-English natural language at UCSD with C- or better; or (3) AP score of 4+ in a non-English language. Native speakers may petition for English to count. Terminal-course demonstration is the 4th-quarter course (e.g. SPAN/FREN/etc. 3 in UCSD's 1-2-3 first-year sequences, or equivalent). No fixed course set.

buckets.label: One introductory course in phonetics, phonology, or morphology
One introductory course in syntax, semantics, or pragmatics
Area distribution: one course from each of two of three areas
buckets.note: One course from each of TWO of the three areas: Computational Linguistics (117, 165, 167, 168, 169); Crosslinguistic Variation (108, 139, 141, 142, 143, 148, 152, 177); Language and Cognition (119, 148, 154, 155, 170, 171, 179, 180, 181). Language and Society is the specialization focus, covered below.

buckets.label: One sociolinguistics course
buckets.note: From the Language and Society area (LIGN 146, 174, 175, 177, or 178).

buckets.label: Linguistics electives emphasizing social dimensions of language
buckets.note: Three linguistics electives; particularly relevant courses per the catalog are LIGN 146, 174, 175, 176, 177, 178.

buckets.label: Upper-division courses in a related social-science department
buckets.note: Two upper-division courses from approved lists in Anthropology, Communication, Cognitive Science, Sociology, Education, or Ethnic Studies. Two APPROPRIATE upper-division courses (language-related) in other departments, per catalog 'especially the Departments of Anthropology, Communication, Cognitive Science, or Sociology'; Education (EDS) and Ethnic Studies (ETHN) are also cited as sources of qualifying language-and-society courses. Ranges are upper-division (100-199) placeholders — the actual qualifying set is only the language/society-relevant courses within these subjects and requires Linguistics adviser approval, so this is not an unrestricted 'any 100-199' list. Anthropology at UCSD splits into ANTH plus sub-codes; ANSC (sociocultural anthropology) is where most language courses live, so both ANTH and ANSC are included.
